standard.title: Language reflects cultural practices
standard.description: notice that people use language in ways that reflect cultural practices
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored connections between language and culture and identified cultural practices associated with the target language (AC9LCHF03). They have recognised that language carries cultural meaning in everyday interactions (AC9LCH2C04). They have not yet systematically noticed how language use across a community reflects cultural practices, values and identity — or compared their own community's language use with others'.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students notice that people use language in ways that reflect cultural practices — including how language use differs across communities, the role of cultural symbols and language in identity, and the relationship between language and cultural belonging.

nodes.label: Language use across communities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify ways in which language use differs across different communities and contexts where the target language is spoken.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two communities or regions where the target language is spoken and describe at least one way language use differs across them — for example, greeting conventions, vocabulary differences, or dialect features.
nodes.typical_width: Compare and contrast classroom language use with target language use in other communities; identify countries and regions where the target language is used; notice that the same language is used differently across communities; explore how language varies across contexts within the target language community.
wider: Research how the target language is used in different countries or regions — identify specific words, expressions or conventions that differ across communities and discuss why
Compare how First Nations Australian languages and the target language are each associated with specific communities and places — discuss what language tells us about belonging and connection
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that language use varies across communities is the conceptual prerequisite for all subsequent work on language, culture and identity. Students who assume all target language speakers use language the same way cannot appreciate the role of cultural context in shaping communication.

response_modes.reason: Community language variation is understood through encounter with varied examples — images, media, guest speakers, maps. Single examples of target language use give an incomplete picture. Varied community contexts build the insight that language is socially and culturally situated.

success_criteria: Names at least two communities or regions where the target language is spoken
Identifies at least one way language use differs across those communities

nodes.label: Cultural symbols, practices and language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify cultural symbols and practices associated with the target language and describe how language is used in those contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two cultural symbols or practices associated with the target language and describe the language used in connection with each.
nodes.typical_width: Explore cultural symbols and practices — festivals, art forms, games, crafts, community events — and the language associated with them; compare target language cultural practices with those of other communities in the class; discuss the role of language in cultural expression and identity.
wider: Examine a cultural practice in depth — identify all the language used in connection with it (greetings, wishes, descriptions, instructions) and explain what the language reveals about the cultural values behind the practice

Compare a cultural practice from the target language community with a similar practice in another community represented in the class — identify where the practices and their associated language are similar or different

response_modes.reason: Cultural symbol and practice knowledge is built through accumulation — students need encounter with varied practices (festivals, arts, games, food, crafts) before the connection between language and cultural practice becomes generalisable. Each encounter adds to the repertoire from which the broader insight emerges.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners carry authentic cultural knowledge — participation in festivals, family practices, community events — that peers may not share. Width investment in tasks that activate and value this knowledge positions students as cultural contributors and builds the connection between their lived experience and academic language learning.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two cultural symbols or practices associated with the target language
Describes at least one piece of language used in connection with a cultural practice

nodes.label: Language, identity and personal connection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on the role of the target language in their own identity and daily life, and share information about their family's language history and cultural connections.
nodes.minimum_width: Share at least two ways the target language is part of their own life — family, community, cultural events, food, travel — and identify at least one language they or family members speak.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss the role of the target language in their own lives — family connections, participation in cultural events, food, community; share information about family languages and cultural backgrounds; reflect on what it means to belong to more than one language community.
wider: Create a personal language map or family language tree — showing which languages are spoken in their family and community, where, and in which contexts
Interview a family member or community elder about their language history and share what they learn with the class — reflecting on how language connects people to place, family and community

response_modes.reason: Personal identity reflection integrates community language awareness (node 1) and cultural practice knowledge (node 2) into a personally grounded connection. The teaching investment is in creating a genuinely inclusive, curious environment where students are invited to share their own language stories without pressure to conform to any single cultural narrative.

success_criteria: Shares at least two personal connections to the target language — family, community, cultural practice or travel
Can identify the languages spoken in their family and describe at least one context where the target language is used
